name: Aged Sheng Puer

origin.subregion: stored in Yunnan, Guangdong, or Taiwan

categoryNote: Chinese 黑茶, “black tea”, is not English black tea (红茶). Puer’s relationship to the dark class is contested; this atlas files it here by process.
pluckStandard: pressed cake aged a decade or more

transformation.note: Fifteen years of slow change after sha qing. Enzymatic oxidation is not the main part of it.

processing.description: The extra “process” is time: slow oxidation, polymerisation, microbial change.
Dry-stored vs traditionally damper southern storage produce different profiles.

profile.mouthfeel: velvet, much less bite than young sheng

rinses.notes: quick rinse; aged cakes still want a wash

decoction.when: after the gongfu session, or as a separate pot
decoction.notes: 煮茶 — simmer the spent leaf. Dark teas can take a boil; this is the extra cup the name 第四泡 points at.

water.note: Fully boiling, mineral-okay. Aged cakes like heat.

storage: Keep the storage style stable; do not fridge. Cakes continue to evolve.

shelfLife.note: Most teas are food. A few teas are projects.

summary: The same raw cake after years: camphor, plum, and a softer body — storage is the craft.
